title: Kerala High Court Upholds Automatic Revocation of a Christian's Will on Marriage Under Section 69
case_name: Suo Motu Civil Reference (on a reference from a Sub Court, Punalur) re validity of Section 69, Indian Succession Act, 1925, with connected petitions including O.P.(C) No. 903 of 2026 and W.P.(C) No. 27213 of 2017
card_summary: A Division Bench of Justices Sathish Ninan and P. Krishna Kumar upheld Section 69 of the Indian Succession Act, which revokes a Christian's will automatically on marriage. The bench held the provision does not breach Articles 14 or 15 by excluding Hindus, since Hindus already get similar protection under the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act. It found no conflict with Section 20 of the same Act either.
card_tip: Any Christian client marrying after executing a will needs a fresh will; the existing one lapses by operation of Section 69 and intestacy rules take over unless a new will is made after the marriage.
verification_notes: Decision date, bench composition and the holding on Articles 14/15 and Section 20 cross-checked across LiveLaw, Verdictum and LawChakra reports of the same judgment; citation 2026:KER:77525 and LiveLaw neutral citation 571 both correspond to the week of 12-18 October 2026.
